docs.title: SRv6 on FRRouting (FRR)
docs.text: FRRouting is an open-source routing suite that provides SRv6 support through its zebra, IS-IS, BGP and static daemons. FRR programs the Linux kernel seg6/seg6local data plane over netlink, so it can only use the SRv6 behaviors the kernel implements.

docs.title: SRv6 Support Status
docs.text:
Feature Status FRR Version BGP SRv6 L3VPN, VPNv6 (End.DT6) 8.1+ BGP SRv6 L3VPN, VPNv4 (End.DT4) 8.3+ Per-VRF End.DT46 SID; SRv6 uSID (behavior usid) for BGP services 8.5+ IS-IS SRv6 (RFC 9352): locators, End/uN and End.X/uA SIDs; static SRv6 segment routes (IPv6) 9.1+ SRv6 static SIDs (uN, uDT4/6/46) 10.3+ Static uA, H.Encaps.Red (staticd and BGP), PSP flavor (End only), IPv4 static segment routes 10.4+ Multiple SRv6 locators / locator per VRF 10.5+ MPLS and SRv6 coexistence on the same L3VRF 10.5+ Global (default-VRF) IPv4/IPv6 unicast over SRv6 core (RFC 9252) 10.6+ BGP-LS (RFC 9552) with SRv6 extensions (RFC 9514) 10.7+ Shared uDT46 SID for the global table 10.7+ EVPN over SRv6 L3 EVPN (RT5) merged for 10.8, not yet released SRv6 TI-LFA, SRv6 Flex-Algo isisd TI-LFA and Flex-Algo are SR-MPLS only OSPFv3 SRv6, PCEP / SR policies for SRv6 ospf6d has no SRv6; pathd is MPLS-based

FRR's SRv6 history starts in 8.1 (zebra SRv6 locator manager and BGP L3VPN for VPNv6). VPNv4 followed in 8.3 and uSID in 8.5 (behavior usid locators, PR #12219); IS-IS learned SRv6 in 9.1. 10.3 (March 2025) added static SRv6 SIDs, 10.4 (July 2025) static uA, H.Encaps.Red and the PSP flavor, and 10.5 (November 2025) multiple-locator support, per-VRF locator selection, and MPLS/SRv6 coexistence for migration scenarios. Release 10.6 also added IPv6 VTEPs for EVPN, but that is EVPN over VXLAN, not SRv6. The SRv6 Support Matrix compares FRR with the kernel and vendor routers behavior by behavior.

FRR 10.6 (March 2026) extends SRv6 beyond VPNs: BGP can now carry global IPv4 and IPv6 unicast over an SRv6 core in the default VRF, the "Global IPv4/IPv6 over SRv6 Core" services of RFC 9252. Per the implementing pull request, the default-VRF service uses DT4/DT6 SIDs and requires the sr0 interface to install the DT routes because of a kernel limitation.

FRR 10.7 (July 2026) brings FRR into controller-driven SRv6 TE: it adds BGP-LS (RFC 9552) with the SRv6 extensions of RFC 9514 — SRv6 Capabilities and Locator TLVs, SRv6 SID NLRI for End, End.X and LAN End.X SIDs, and the Endpoint Behavior and SID Structure TLVs. Static SRv6 SIDs configured in zebra can be exported into BGP-LS so a TE controller sees them. The 10.7 changelog also adds a single uDT46 SID for the global table as an alternative to separate uDT4/uDT6 SIDs.

docs.title: Global table over SRv6 (10.6+)
docs.text:
router bgp 65001
 segment-routing srv6
  locator MAIN
 exit
 neighbor 2001:db8::2 remote-as 65001
 !
 address-family ipv6 unicast
  sid export auto
  neighbor 2001:db8::2 activate
  neighbor 2001:db8::2 encapsulation-srv6
 exit-address-family

sid export (default VRF only) allocates the global-table service SID; compare sid vpn export for L3VPN. encapsulation-srv6 makes BGP attach the Prefix-SID attribute toward that neighbor (encapsulation-srv6-relax sends routes with and without it). Command names are from the FRR 10.6 BGP user guide — check the docs for your release before deploying.

docs.title: Configuration Example
docs.text:
! Enable SRv6 in IS-IS
router isis CORE
 segment-routing srv6
  locator MAIN
 exit

! Define SRv6 locator
segment-routing
 srv6
  locators
   locator MAIN
    prefix fc00:0:1::/48 block-len 32 node-len 16 func-bits 16
   exit
  exit
 exit

docs.title: SRv6 on Juniper Junos
docs.text:
Juniper implements SRv6 in Junos OS (MX Series) and Junos OS Evolved (PTX and ACX7000 Series), with both full-length (classic) SIDs and micro-SIDs (uSID, the RFC 9800 NEXT-CSID flavor). This guide walks through a complete uSID deployment — locator, IS-IS, L3VPN and Internet services, Flex-Algo and TI-LFA — following the structure of Juniper's validated design for SRv6 core and edge, and shows the commands to verify each step.

Juniper Validated Design

The JVD for Service Provider SRv6 Core and Edge was qualified on Junos 24.4R2 and Junos Evolved 24.4R2 with MX480 (MPC7E, MPC10E), MX10004 (LC9600), MX2010 (MPC11E), MX304 and PTX10002-36QDD. It uses uSID only (F3216 format, blocks from 5f00::/16), Flex-Algo 0/128/129, TI-LFA with microloop avoidance, uDT46 L3VPN and uDX2 EVPN-VPWS.

docs.title: Platforms and Releases
docs.text:
Capability Junos OS (MX) Junos OS Evolved SRv6 in IS-IS, classic SIDs 20.3R1 (MX240/480/960/2000; MPC7E/8E/9E or newer; per TechLibrary — Feature Explorer lists MX960 at 21.1R1) PTX10002-36QDD 24.2R2, PTX10008 24.4R1-S2 L3 services over SRv6 (BGP) 20.4R1 (MX and vMX); MX304 22.2R3; MX10004 22.3R1 PTX10002-36QDD 24.2R2; PTX10008 24.4R1-S2 uSID in IS-IS transport 23.4R1 (MX204 through MX10016) PTX10008 24.4R1-S2 uSID with L3VPN and IS-IS on ACX — ACX7024/7100/7509 23.2R1; ACX7024X/7332/7348 23.4R1 uSID with TI-LFA, microloop avoidance, Flex-Algo 23.4R1 ACX7024X/7348 24.2R1 SRv6 Flex-Algo Classic SIDs 20.3R1 (inter-level leaking 21.2R1); uSID 23.4R1 ACX7024/7100/7509 23.1R1 SRv6 microloop avoidance (IS-IS) 21.1R1 PTX10002-36QDD 24.4R1

Release numbers are the "introduced" values from Juniper Feature Explorer or, where noted, Juniper TechLibrary; check Feature Explorer for your exact platform and line card. Later additions include static and PCEP SRv6-TE policies (MX 21.3R1), EVPN E-LAN over SRv6 (MX 23.4R1), the End.B6.Encaps binding SID (ACX7000 25.2R1, MX 26.2R1) and TWAMP performance measurement over SRv6 paths (PTX 24.4R1). The SRv6 Support Matrix compares Junos with other platforms feature by feature. cRPD supports SRv6 in IS-IS and L3 services in BGP with limitations (no flavor or Flex-Algo options on End SIDs, no ARM64). There is no official SRv6 support statement for vJunos-router.

docs.title: Building Blocks
docs.text:
Junos object Hierarchy What it is Block routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 block The uSID block (default 32 bits, the only length on ACX), with global (GIB) and local (LIB) ID ranges Locator routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator The node's /48 (with micro-sid) or classic locator; can be bound to a Flex-Algo uN / End SID protocols isis source-packet-routing srv6 locator <name> micro-node-sid Advertised by IS-IS; without it the local locator is not even installed uA / End.X SID protocols isis interface <ifl> level 2 srv6-adjacency-segment Per-adjacency SID, protected or unprotected Service SID routing-instances <vrf> protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator <name> uDT4/uDT6/uDT46 (or End.DT4/6/46) per VRF

The default uSID length is 16 bits. In each block the GIB defaults to 0x0000–0xDFFF (static) and the LIB to 0xE000–0xFFFF (dynamic). With no flavor configured, micro-sid SIDs use PSP and USD.

docs.title: Step 1: Platform Prerequisites (MX)
docs.text:
set chassis network-services enhanced-ip
set routing-options resolution preserve-nexthop-hierarchy
set routing-options forwarding-table srv6-chain-merge

enhanced-ip is needed on MX only. The other two enable the chained, hierarchical next-hop structures that SRv6 services resolve through; the JVD sets them on every router.

docs.title: Step 2: uSID Block and Locator
docs.text:
The example uses the IANA SRv6 SID block 5f00::/16 (RFC 9602), block 5f00::/32 and node 1 = 5f00:0:1::/48 (F3216: 32-bit block, 16-bit node uSID, 16-bit function).

set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 block BLK0 5f00::/32
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 block BLK0 local-micro-sid maximum-static-sids 2000
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 5f00:0:1::/48
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 micro-sid block-name BLK0

maximum-static-sids reserves part of the LIB for statically configured service SIDs. By default the static LIB range is empty, so any static micro-dt46-sid value would fail to commit. Changing GIB/LIB sizes later is disruptive (it requires restarting routing, and dynamic SIDs can change), so size it up front. Use the same block on every router; uSID compression only works between nodes that share a block.

Classic (full-length) SIDs instead of uSID 

set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator myloc 2001:db8:0:a0::/64
set protocols isis source-packet-routing srv6 locator myloc end-sid 2001:db8:0:a0:d01:: flavor usd
set protocols isis interface xe-0/0/0:0.0 level 2 srv6-adjacency-segment protected locator myloc end-x-sid 2001:db8:0:a0:1a01:: flavor psp
End and End.X SIDs must fall inside the locator prefix or the commit fails. Encapsulation defaults to a reduced SRH; set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 no-reduced-srh restores the full SRH (on ACX7000 this restarts the PFE).

docs.title: Step 3: IS-IS
docs.text:
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 point-to-point
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 level 2 srv6-adjacency-segment unprotected locator LOC0 micro-adjacency-sid
set protocols isis interface lo0.0 passive
set protocols isis source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 micro-node-sid
set protocols isis level 1 disable
set protocols isis level 2 wide-metrics-only
  • micro-node-sid advertises the locator and the uN SID (RFC 9352 SRv6 Locator TLV). The locator must be configured under IS-IS even if you only want SRv6 for L3VPN.
  • micro-adjacency-sid with no value allocates a dynamic uA from the LIB. The JVD uses unprotected uA SIDs and relies on TI-LFA to protect uN SIDs and prefixes.
  • IS-IS multi-topology (set protocols isis topologies ipv6-unicast) is not required. The JVD only uses it during migration, so IPv4 SR-MPLS and IPv6 SRv6 topologies can differ.

docs.title: Step 4: L3VPN over SRv6
docs.text:
On each PE, assign a service SID per VRF and enable SRv6 service signaling on the BGP families.

# VRF with a dynamic uDT46 SID (End.DT46 with NEXT-CSID)
set routing-instances CUST-A instance-type vrf
set routing-instances CUST-A interface ge-0/0/2.0
set routing-instances CUST-A route-distinguisher 192.0.2.1:100
set routing-instances CUST-A vrf-target target:65000:100
set routing-instances CUST-A protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 micro-dt46-sid
#   or a static value from the LIB static range:  ... micro-dt46-sid 0xfc30
#   or per address family:                         ... micro-dt4-sid / micro-dt6-sid
#   classic SIDs:                                  ... locator myloc end-dt4-sid / end-dt6-sid / end-dt46-sid <sid>

# IBGP to the route reflectors (IPv6 transport)
set protocols bgp group RR type internal
set protocols bgp group RR local-address 2001:db8:ff::11
set protocols bgp group RR family inet-vpn unicast extended-nexthop
set protocols bgp group RR family inet-vpn unicast advertise-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet-vpn unicast accept-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet6-vpn unicast advertise-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet6-vpn unicast accept-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family route-target nexthop-resolution no-resolution
set protocols bgp group RR neighbor 2001:db8:ff::1
set protocols bgp rfc8950-compliant
set protocols bgp multipath list-nexthop

How it resolves: with SRv6 services enabled, Junos ignores the BGP NEXT_HOP for resolution and resolves the route on the locator inside the SRv6 SID, which IS-IS has installed in inet6.3 as an SRV6-ISIS route. No resolution rib tweaks are needed. Two details matter in practice:

  • extended-nexthop and rfc8950-compliant make VPN-IPv4 routes carry IPv6 next hops in the standard (RFC 8950) encoding, which matters for interoperability with other vendors.
  • Route-target (RT-constraint) routes otherwise stay hidden, because the PE loopbacks exist only in inet6.0. nexthop-resolution no-resolution fixes this.

The per-VRF SID is advertised in the BGP Prefix-SID attribute (SRv6 L3 Service TLV) with the function bits transposed into the label field, as described in RFC 9252. Inter-AS Option C works over SRv6; Option B over SRv6 is not supported. For SIDs learned only via BGP (no IGP route to the remote locator), Junos 24.2R1+ on MX can use routing-options dynamic-tunnels <name> srv6.

docs.title: Internet (Global Table) over SRv6
docs.text:
set protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC0 micro-dt46-sid
set protocols bgp group RR family inet unicast extended-nexthop
set protocols bgp group RR family inet unicast advertise-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet unicast accept-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet6 unicast advertise-srv6-service
set protocols bgp group RR family inet6 unicast accept-srv6-service

Filter your SID block at the border

The JVD filters 5f00::/16 (and more-specifics) on eBGP sessions. If another AS can inject routes covering your SID space, it can attract SRv6-encapsulated VPN traffic. See Security.

docs.title: Step 5: Flex-Algo
docs.text:
A Flex-Algo needs a definition, IS-IS participation and its own locator. Services pick the algorithm through the locator their SID comes from.

# Algorithm 128 = low-latency
set routing-options flex-algorithm 128 definition metric-type delay-metric
set routing-options flex-algorithm 128 definition spf
set protocols isis source-packet-routing flex-algorithm 128

# Locator for algorithm 128, in its own /32 block
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 block BLK128 5f00:a1::/32
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 5f00:a1:1::/48
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 algorithm 128
set routing-options source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 micro-sid block-name BLK128
set protocols isis source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 micro-node-sid
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 level 2 srv6-adjacency-segment unprotected locator LOC128 micro-adjacency-sid

# Option A: the whole VRF uses the low-latency locator
set routing-instances CUST-LL protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 micro-dt46-sid

# Option B: allocate a second SID in a VRF and select it per prefix by policy
set routing-instances CUST-A protocols bgp source-packet-routing srv6 locator LOC128 micro-dt46-sid non-default
set policy-options community VOICE members 65000:911
set policy-options policy-statement LL-PREFIXES term VOICE from community VOICE
set policy-options policy-statement LL-PREFIXES term VOICE then srv6 locator LOC128 micro-dt46-sid
set policy-options policy-statement LL-PREFIXES term VOICE then accept
set protocols bgp group RR export LL-PREFIXES

In option B the VRF advertises its default SID for most prefixes, and the export policy on the IBGP group swaps in the algorithm-128 SID for the matching ones, so remote PEs reach those prefixes over the low-latency topology.

Delay-based algorithms need link delay: enable delay-measurement on the IS-IS interfaces (TWAMP Light), and advertise it as an application-specific link attribute for Flex-Algo. IS-IS installs SIDs of non-zero algorithms in inet6color.0. On Junos, Flex-Algo participation applies to SR-MPLS and SRv6 together — you cannot define an algorithm for SRv6 only. See Flex-Algorithm.

docs.title: Step 6: TI-LFA and Microloop Avoidance
docs.text:
set protocols isis backup-spf-options use-post-convergence-lfa
set protocols isis backup-spf-options use-source-packet-routing
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 level 2 post-convergence-lfa
set protocols isis interface et-0/0/0.0 level 2 post-convergence-lfa node-protection cost 16777214
set protocols isis spf-options microloop-avoidance post-convergence-path delay 5000

Link protection is the default once post-convergence-lfa is on an interface. The JVD adds node protection with a very high cost, so the node-protecting path is preferred but a link-protecting backup is still used when no node-protecting path exists. uSID-based TI-LFA, microloop avoidance and Flex-Algo protection arrived in Junos 23.4R1. Before Junos 26.2R1, SRLG is not considered for SRv6 TI-LFA; 26.2R1 adds IS-IS IPv6 SRLG (TLV 139) for SRLG-aware TI-LFA on MX, PTX and ACX7000. The JVD measured worst-case link-failure convergence around 5 ms. See TI-LFA for the algorithm.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Command What to look for show isis overview SRv6: Enabled, the locator and algorithm, micro-node-SID … Flavor: PSP, USD, post-convergence backup and microloop avoidance state show isis adjacency extensive SRv6 unprotected END-X-SID … with its flavor, per adjacency show isis database <router> extensive \| find SRv6 SRv6 Locator TLV (MTID, algorithm), uN SID with block/node lengths, SRv6 MSDs, End.X SIDs show srv6 block BLK0 GIB/LIB ranges, static and dynamic SID counts show route table inet6.3 protocol isis Remote locators and SIDs as SRV6-ISIS routes with SRV6-Tunnel next hops show route table inet6.0 protocol srv6 Local service SIDs, e.g. a uDT46 SID pointing to table CUST-A.inet.0 show route receive-protocol bgp <rr> table CUST-A detail SRv6 SID: … Behavior: 63 BL:32 NL:16 FL:16 AL:0 TL:16 TO:48 (63 = End.DT4 with NEXT-CSID) show route table CUST-A.inet.0 <prefix> extensive SRV6-Tunnel: Reduced-SRH Encap-mode, the segment list and Protocol next hop: <remote locator> show isis backup coverage Percentage of nodes and prefixes protected, per topology show isis backup spf results Backup path per destination (add no-coverage to list unprotected ones) ping srv6 isis <sid> / traceroute srv6 isis <sid> SRv6 OAM reachability of a uN or End SID

show spring-traffic-engineering is for SR-TE policies, not for SRv6 locators and service SIDs.

docs.title: Limits and Gotchas
docs.text:
• SID depth (from the Junos SRv6 docs): MX encapsulates up to 6 SIDs and inserts up to 5; ACX7000 encapsulates 12 and inserts 10; PTX10002-36QDD and PTX10008 (Express 5) support 7. uSID packs up to six 16-bit uSIDs per 128-bit container, which leaves plenty of headroom for TE and TI-LFA.
  • Encap vs insert: ingress PEs always encapsulate, so egress SIDs must support USD; transit SRH insertion for TI-LFA needs a PSP-capable last SID.
  • Static plus IS-IS SIDs: configuring the same static uA or End.X SID under both the SRv6 manager and IS-IS fails commit (a duplicate uN is allowed; IS-IS wins).
  • IS-IS SRv6 limits: the IS-IS SRv6 concept page lists anycast locators, SRLG, End.X interface groups and Flex-Algo locator conflict resolution as unsupported. Feature Explorer has since added anycast locators and summarization (MX10004/MX10008 22.3R1, ACX7000 22.4R1) and SRLG (26.2R1), so check your platform and release.
  • No next-hop-self knob: Junos IBGP needs an export policy with then next-hop self when you redistribute CE routes into plain IPv4/IPv6 BGP.

docs.title: SRv6 on Linux
docs.text: The Linux kernel has had native SRv6 since 4.10 (February 2017; seg6local endpoint behaviors since 4.14) and is one of the most complete open-source SRv6 data planes. Everything is configured with iproute2: seg6 routes act as headends (H.Encaps and friends), and seg6local routes bind local SIDs to endpoint behaviors (End, End.X, End.DT4, …). Routing daemons such as FRRouting program the same kernel objects, so what you learn here applies to FRR, SONiC hosts and container labs alike.

docs.title: Behavior Support by Kernel Version
docs.text: First mainline release containing each feature, checked against the kernel git history (latest release: 7.3, October 2026). Distribution and stable kernels may carry fixes earlier; features also need a matching iproute2.

docs.title: Headend behaviors (ip route ... encap seg6 mode ...)
docs.text: RFC 8986 behavior iproute2 mode Kernel Notes H.Encaps encap 4.10 IPv6 or IPv4 payload SRH insertion (not in RFC 8986) inline 4.10 Adds an SRH to an IPv6 packet in place H.Encaps.L2 l2encap 4.14 Ethernet payload H.Encaps.Red encap.red 6.0 iproute2 6.0 H.Encaps.L2.Red l2encap.red 6.0 iproute2 6.0 Per-route outer source (tunsrc) ... tunsrc <addr> 7.1 iproute2 7.1; overrides the per-namespace ip sr tunsrc

docs.title: Endpoint behaviors (ip -6 route ... encap seg6local action ...)
docs.text: Behavior Kernel Notes End 4.14 seg6local itself arrived in 4.14 End.X 4.14 Optional oif for link-local next hops from 6.17 End.T 4.14 table N End.DX2 4.14 oif <dev>; no VLAN variant (End.DX2V) End.DX4 / End.DX6 4.14 nh4 / nh6 End.DT6 4.14 (table), 5.11 (vrftable) VRF mode needs net.vrf.strict_mode=1 End.DT4 5.11 vrftable only; needs VRF strict mode End.DT46 5.14 vrftable; needs VRF strict mode End.B6 (SRH insertion) 4.14 srh segs ... End.B6.Encaps 4.14 srh segs ... End.BPF 4.18 Attach an eBPF program as the behavior PSP flavor 6.3 End only (flavors psp) NEXT-C-SID flavor (uSID) 6.1 (End), 6.6 (End.X) flavors next-csid lblen 32 nflen 16 (defaults 32/16) Per-SID counters 5.13 count; iproute2 5.14

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text:
Feature Kernel Notes SRH processing, seg6_enabled sysctl 4.10 Per interface; see Troubleshooting HMAC TLV, seg6_require_hmac, ip sr hmac 4.10 Constant-time MAC compare from 6.17 ip sr tunsrc (per-namespace outer source) 4.10 Default :: = pick from the egress interface net.ipv6.seg6_flowlabel 4.18 Compute the outer flow label for encapsulated traffic Netfilter hooks on seg6/seg6local 5.15 Off by default; net.netfilter.nf_hooks_lwtunnel=1 Post-encapsulation lookup in a chosen FIB table 7.3 SEG6_IPTUNNEL_TABLE; iproute2 support not yet in a release

Not implemented in the kernel

End.DX2V, End.DT2U, End.DT2M, End.B6.Encaps.Red, the USP and USD flavors, REPLACE-C-SID and every RFC 9433 mobile behavior. End.BM, End.S, End.AS and End.AM exist as names in the UAPI and in iproute2, but the kernel has no implementation behind them. For EVPN (End.DT2U/DT2M), use FRRouting with a VXLAN data plane or a vendor router. For MUP behaviors, use an eBPF data plane such as Vinbero.

docs.title: iproute2 Recipes
docs.text: Every command on this page was tested on kernel 6.12 with iproute2 6.9. Behavior names follow RFC 8986; in iproute2 they are the action keyword of a seg6local route.

docs.title: Headend: steering traffic into SRv6 (seg6)
docs.text:
# H.Encaps: IPv4 prefix into an outer IPv6 header + SRH with two segments
ip route add 198.51.100.0/24 encap seg6 mode encap \
    segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::a4 dev eth0

# H.Encaps.Red: same, but the first SID is only in the DA (SRH one entry shorter;
# with a single SID there is no SRH at all)
ip route add 198.51.101.0/24 encap seg6 mode encap.red \
    segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::a4 dev eth0

# uSID: one container carrying uN(3) uN(4) uDT4 — no SRH needed
ip route add 198.51.102.0/24 encap seg6 mode encap \
    segs fcbb:bb00:300:400:e004:: dev eth0

# SRH insertion into an existing IPv6 packet (not an RFC 8986 behavior)
ip -6 route add 2001:db8:99::/48 encap seg6 mode inline segs fc00:0:3::1 dev eth0

# H.Encaps.L2 / H.Encaps.L2.Red: frames received for this route are carried as Ethernet payload
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::12/128 encap seg6 mode l2encap segs fc00:0:4::d2 dev eth1
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::13/128 encap seg6 mode l2encap.red segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::d2 dev eth1

The outer source address comes from ip sr tunsrc set <addr> (one per network namespace); if it is unset, the kernel picks a source address of the outgoing interface. Kernel and iproute2 7.1 add a per-route tunsrc <addr> option that overrides it.

docs.title: Endpoint behaviors (seg6local)
docs.text:
# End (node SID), optionally with the PSP flavor (6.3+)
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::1/128 encap seg6local action End dev eth0
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::2/128 encap seg6local action End flavors psp dev eth0

# End.X (adjacency SID) toward a specific IPv6 next hop
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1:e001::/64 encap seg6local action End.X nh6 2001:db8:1::2 dev eth0

# End.T: next segment looked up in table 10
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::3/128 encap seg6local action End.T table 10 dev eth0

# End.DX4 / End.DX6: decapsulate and cross-connect to a next hop (per-CE VPN)
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::d4/128 encap seg6local action End.DX4 nh4 192.0.2.2 dev eth1
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::d6/128 encap seg6local action End.DX6 nh6 2001:db8:2::2 dev eth1

# End.DX2: decapsulate and send the inner Ethernet frame out of eth1
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::d2/128 encap seg6local action End.DX2 oif eth1 dev eth1

# End.B6 (SRH insertion) and End.B6.Encaps: binding SIDs for an SR policy
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::b6/128 encap seg6local action End.B6 srh segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::1 dev eth0
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::b7/128 encap seg6local action End.B6.Encaps srh segs fc00:0:3::1,fc00:0:4::1 dev eth0

# Per-SID counters (read with: ip -s -6 route show fc00:0:1::c)
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::c/128 encap seg6local action End count dev eth0

docs.title: VRF decapsulation: End.DT4, End.DT6, End.DT46
docs.text:
The table-lookup behaviors deliver the inner packet into a VRF. Create the VRF first and enable strict mode; without it the kernel rejects any vrftable SID with Error: Strict mode for VRF is disabled.

ip link add vrf-red type vrf table 10
ip link set vrf-red up
sysctl -w net.vrf.strict_mode=1      # the sysctl appears once the vrf module is loaded

ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::a4/128  encap seg6local action End.DT4  vrftable 10 dev vrf-red
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::a6/128  encap seg6local action End.DT6  vrftable 10 dev vrf-red
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::a46/128 encap seg6local action End.DT46 vrftable 10 dev vrf-red

# legacy End.DT6 form without a VRF device: plain table lookup
ip -6 route add fc00:0:1::a7/128 encap seg6local action End.DT6 table 10 dev eth0

docs.title: Compressed SIDs: NEXT-C-SID (uSID)
docs.text:
# uN: End with the NEXT-C-SID flavor (6.1+), 32-bit block + 16-bit node uSID
ip -6 route add fcbb:bb00:100::/48 encap seg6local action End \
    flavors next-csid lblen 32 nflen 16 dev eth0

# uA: End.X with NEXT-C-SID (6.6+)
ip -6 route add fcbb:bb00:100:e001::/64 encap seg6local action End.X nh6 2001:db8:1::2 \
    flavors next-csid lblen 32 nflen 16 dev eth0

lblen is the locator-block length and nflen the node + function length (both in bits, multiples of 8). See uSID Compression for how the destination address is shifted at each hop.

docs.title: Lab: Two Routers in Network Namespaces
docs.text:
A self-contained L3VPN over SRv6 between two network namespaces, r1 and r2. Each has a customer VRF (table 100) with a dummy "LAN", an End.DT46 SID for the VRF, and an H.Encaps.Red route toward the other side. Static routes for the locators stand in for IS-IS. Run as root on any recent kernel:

srv6-lab.sh
#!/bin/sh
set -e
ip netns add r1
ip netns add r2
ip link add veth1 netns r1 type veth peer name veth2 netns r2

for r in r1 r2; do
  ip -n $r link set lo up
  ip -n $r link add vrf-cust type vrf table 100
  ip -n $r link set vrf-cust up
  ip -n $r link add cust0 type dummy
  ip -n $r link set cust0 master vrf-cust up
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.all.seg6_enabled=1
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.vrf.strict_mode=1
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0
  ip netns exec $r sysctl -qw net.ipv4.conf.vrf-cust.rp_filter=0
done
ip netns exec r1 sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.veth1.seg6_enabled=1
ip netns exec r2 sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.veth2.seg6_enabled=1

ip -n r1 link set veth1 up
ip -n r2 link set veth2 up
ip -n r1 -6 addr add 2001:db8:12::1/64 dev veth1 nodad
ip -n r2 -6 addr add 2001:db8:12::2/64 dev veth2 nodad
ip -n r1 addr add 10.1.1.1/24 dev cust0
ip -n r2 addr add 10.2.2.2/24 dev cust0

# Locators: r1 = fc00:0:1::/48, r2 = fc00:0:2::/48
ip -n r1 -6 route add fc00:0:2::/48 via 2001:db8:12::2
ip -n r2 -6 route add fc00:0:1::/48 via 2001:db8:12::1

# Service SIDs: End.DT46 into the customer VRF
ip -n r1 -6 route add fc00:0:1::d46/128 encap seg6local action End.DT46 vrftable 100 dev vrf-cust
ip -n r2 -6 route add fc00:0:2::d46/128 encap seg6local action End.DT46 vrftable 100 dev vrf-cust

# Headend: H.Encaps.Red from the VRF toward the remote End.DT46 SID
ip -n r1 route add 10.2.2.0/24 vrf vrf-cust encap seg6 mode encap.red segs fc00:0:2::d46 dev veth1
ip -n r2 route add 10.1.1.0/24 vrf vrf-cust encap seg6 mode encap.red segs fc00:0:1::d46 dev veth2

ip netns exec r1 ping -c 3 -I vrf-cust 10.2.2.2

Watch the encapsulated traffic on r2 while pinging. With a single SID and encap.red, there is no SRH: the outer header's next header is 4 (IPv4).

# ip netns exec r2 tcpdump -nvi veth2 'ip6[6] == 4'
IP6 (hlim 64, next-header IPIP (4) payload length: 84) 2001:db8:12::1 > fc00:0:2::d46:
    IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 60488, offset 0, flags [DF], proto ICMP (1), length 84)
    10.1.1.1 > 10.2.2.2: ICMP echo request, id 49, seq 1, length 64

Switch r1 to mode encap and the SRH appears, with one segment and Segments Left 0:

# ip -n r1 route replace 10.2.2.0/24 vrf vrf-cust encap seg6 mode encap segs fc00:0:2::d46 dev veth1
# ip netns exec r2 tcpdump -nvi veth2 'ip6[6] == 43'
IP6 (hlim 64, next-header Routing (43) payload length: 108) 2001:db8:12::1 > fc00:0:2::d46:
    RT6 (len=2, type=4, segleft=0, last-entry=0, flags=0x0, tag=0, [0]fc00:0:2::d46)
    IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, ...) 10.1.1.1 > 10.2.2.2: ICMP echo request, id 54, seq 1, length 64

Clean up with ip netns del r1; ip netns del r2. To grow this into a multi-hop topology with IS-IS and BGP, move to Containerlab with FRR.

A six-namespace version of this lab (two PEs, two P routers, parallel links) produces the SRv6 packet capture library: annotated pcapng files of H.Encaps, H.Encaps.Red, End, End.X, End.DT4/DT6/DT46, End.DX2, NEXT-C-SID, SRH HMAC and source-routed traceroute, with the script to regenerate them.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause Fix Packets with an SRH are dropped on arrival seg6_enabled is 0. The kernel uses the lower of the all value and the receiving interface's value, so both must be 1 sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.seg6_enabled=1 and net.ipv6.conf.<if>.seg6_enabled=1 Transit node does not forward SRv6 traffic IPv6 forwarding disabled sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1 End.DT4/End.DT46 decapsulates, but nothing reaches the VRF and no counter increments Reverse-path filtering on the VRF device. Distributions often set rp_filter (1 or 2) by default; new devices inherit it, and the effective value is the max of all and the device sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.<vrf>.rp_filter=0 (and all) — this was the one failure we hit building the lab above Error: Strict mode for VRF is disabled. when adding End.DT4/DT6/DT46 VRF strict mode off sysctl -w net.vrf.strict_mode=1 (after creating a VRF) Ping from the VRF fails with ip vrf exec in containers ip vrf exec needs cgroup BPF Use ping -I <vrf-device> instead Encapsulated packets leave with an unexpected source No tunsrc set ip sr tunsrc set <addr> Large packets disappear after encapsulation Encapsulation adds 40 bytes (plus 8 + 16 × n for an SRH) Raise the underlay MTU or lower the customer MTU SRH packets dropped on an HMAC-enabled interface seg6_require_hmac = 1 drops packets without a valid HMAC TLV Configure keys with ip sr hmac set on both ends, or use 0 (validate only if present) / -1 (ignore HMAC)

Useful commands:

ip -6 route show | grep seg6local           # local SIDs
ip route show vrf vrf-cust                  # encap routes in a VRF
ip -s -6 route show fc00:0:1::c             # per-SID counters (routes added with "count")
ip -6 route get fc00:0:2::d46               # which route/SID a destination hits
tcpdump -nvi eth0 'ip6 proto 43'            # packets whose first extension header is the SRH
tcpdump -nvi eth0 'ip6[6] == 4 or ip6[6] == 41'  # H.Encaps(.Red) with no SRH (IPv4 / IPv6 inside)
nstat -az | grep -i -E 'Ip6InNoRoutes|Ip6InDiscards|Ip6InHdrErrors'
sysctl -a 2>/dev/null | grep seg6           # seg6_enabled / seg6_require_hmac per interface

Filtering SRv6 in tcpdump

ip6 proto 43 only matches when the SRH directly follows the IPv6 header. Reduced encapsulation with one SID has no SRH at all, so match the payload type (ip6[6] == 4 for IPv4, 41 for IPv6) or the destination prefix (dst net fc00::/16).

docs.title: Not Yet Merged: Mobile User Plane (RFC 9433)
docs.text:
The kernel has no RFC 9433 Mobile User Plane behaviors in any release up to 7.3. Patches from Yuya Kusakabe are under review on netdev (status as of 20 October 2026):

Series Posted Status What it adds net-next "seg6: add SRv6 Mobile User Plane (RFC 9433) behaviors" (7 patches) and the matching iproute2-next series v1 3 May, v2 4 May 2026 Changes requested; superseded End.MAP, End.M.GTP4.E, End.M.GTP6.E, End.M.GTP6.D, End.M.GTP6.D.Di and H.M.GTP4.D RFC net-next "seg6: add support for the SRv6 End.MAP behavior" + selftest v1 10 July → v5 2 October 2026 RFC, not merged End.MAP only: rewrites the IPv6 DA to a configured mapped SID and forwards via the FIB, under a new seg6mobile lightweight-tunnel encap RFC iproute2-next "End.MAP behavior under seg6mobile encap" v5 2 October 2026 RFC, not applied iproute2 support plus a new uapi header seg6_mobile.h

After review of the all-in-one submission, the author split the work into per-behavior series, starting with End.MAP; the GTP-U interworking behaviors (End.M.GTP4.E and friends) would follow separately. An "RFC" posting cannot be merged as is, so End.MAP will not appear before a non-RFC version is accepted into net-next — at the earliest, the release after that. Until then, use an eBPF data plane such as Vinbero for MUP/GTP behaviors.

docs.title: SRv6 on Nokia SR OS
docs.text: Nokia SR OS supports SRv6 in two forms: classic (full-length SIDs per RFC 8986) and micro-segment SRv6 (uSID), which Nokia describes as an extension of the SRv6 network-programming model rather than a replacement. Both can run on the same router at the same time, and Nokia's application note states that uSIDs and classic SIDs can be combined in the same segment list — keeping most of the path compressed while still carrying a full-length service or function SID where needed. SRv6 first shipped in SR OS 21.5.R2 on FP4-based hardware (IS-IS, VPRN, Flex-Algo, LFA/TI-LFA); EVPN-IFL followed in 22.5.R1 and EVPN-VPLS/VPWS and SRv6 policies in 22.7.R1.

docs.title: Key Characteristics
docs.text: Aspect Detail Source SID modes Classic SRv6 and micro-segment SRv6 concurrently on one platform; SIDs of each type must come from different SID blocks SR OS 26.7 user guide Mixing in a segment list uSID containers and classic SIDs can be used together in one segment list Application note Classic SID length Variable: 32-bit, 16-bit or 128-bit Application note uSID container 32-bit block carrying up to six 16-bit uSIDs; uSIDs are global (node) or local (adjacency, service, function) Application note uSID allocation global-sid-entries (default 16) splits the 16-bit space: 0x0000-0x3FFF global, 0x4000-0xFFFF local; block-length must be identical network-wide SR OS 26.7 user guide Maximum SID depth The application note quotes up to 9 classic SIDs or 47 uSIDs including primary path, LFA backup and service SID. The configurable limit per SR policy segment list is 7 classic segments or 24 micro-segments (42 uSIDs with pre-compressed containers) Application note; SR OS 26.7 user guide Coexistence Classic SRv6, uSID and MPLS/SR-MPLS enabled together on the same router, service or IP interface Application note

docs.title: Behaviors (SR OS 26.7)
docs.text: Mode Behaviors Micro-segment uN and uA (advertised by IS-IS); uDT4, uDT6, uDT46, uDX2, uDT2U, uDT2M (BGP services or static) Classic End and End.X (with PSP/USP/USD flavors), End.DT4, End.DT6, End.DT46, End.DX2, End.DT2U, End.DT2M; End.B6.Encaps.Red as the SR policy binding SID Headend H.Encaps.Red and H.Encaps.L2.Red only (plain H.Encaps and H.Encaps.L2 are not supported); H.Insert.Red for LFA repair Not supported End.T, End.DX4, End.DX6

docs.title: Services and Traffic Engineering
docs.text:
Area Supported (classic and uSID) L3 services Base-router BGP routes, VPRN (IP-VPN), EVPN-IFL L2 services EVPN-VPLS and EVPN-VPWS with single-active or all-active multihoming Multicast Tree-SID SRv6 (replication segments) for NG-MVPN I-PMSI/S-PMSI, first documented in 25.3: static CLI configuration, classic SIDs only, no LFA or BFD protection (see Multicast) IGP IS-IS, including Flex-Algo TE Flex-Algo; SRv6 policies configured statically or via the BGP SR Policy address family (22.7.R1), or from a PCE over PCEP (RFC 9603, first documented in 26.7) IGP extras IS-IS MT0 and MT2; microloop avoidance for SRv6 (first documented in 26.3); BGP-LS export of SRv6 information (IS-IS only) OAM Ping and traceroute to SRv6 SIDs, VRF prefixes and SRv6 policies Protection LFA, remote LFA, TI-LFA (link, node, SRLG); SR OS originates and terminates repair tunnels with H.Insert.Red and can terminate H.Encaps.Red repair tunnels from other vendors Gateway Interworking between MPLS, SR-MPLS, SRv6 classic, SRv6 uSID, VXLAN and MPLS-over-UDP at transport and service layers

Multi-vendor TI-LFA

SR OS builds TI-LFA and remote-LFA repair tunnels with H.Insert.Red, while some other implementations use H.Encaps.Red. The SR OS guide describes a termination mode to accept encapsulated repair tunnels — check this when mixing vendors in one IGP domain. See TI-LFA.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text:
The SR OS 26.7 Segment Routing and PCE User Guide's SRv6 chapter applies to the 7450 ESS, 7750 SR, 7950 XRS and VSR. Nokia's advanced configuration guides add the hardware condition: SRv6 "is supported on FP4-based equipment in SR OS Release 21.5.R2 and later", and the EVPN chapters require FP4-based network ports. The application note covers "Nokia routing platforms" generically.

SR Linux (Nokia's data-center NOS) is a separate implementation: its SRv6 chapter first appears in SR Linux 26.3 and lists the 7730 SXR and the 7220 IXR-H5/H6, the latter as basic uSID transit nodes for AI back-end fabrics. EVPN-VPLS (MAC-VRF) over SRv6 is not supported there.

docs.title: SRv6 on SONiC
docs.text: SONiC (Software for Open Networking in the Cloud) has carried SRv6 code since the 202111 release. On a switch, SRv6 forwarding happens in the ASIC: SONiC programs it through orchagent (srv6orch) and the SAI SRv6 objects, so which behaviors actually forward depends on each vendor's SAI implementation.

docs.title: Current Status
docs.text:
Release SRv6 change Source 202111 First orchagent SRv6: End, End.DT46, H.Encaps.Red Release notes 202211 uSID data plane: uN, uA Release notes 202305 Selectable SID-list type (encaps / encaps.red / insert) sonic-swss #2406 202405 Adjacency programming for End.X, uA, End.DX4/DX6 (L3Adj) Release notes 202505 Static SRv6 in CONFIG_DB (uN, uDT46), rated Alpha in the release notes; SRv6 VPN support in srv6orch Release notes, sonic-swss #3293 master (Aug 2026) Static uA in CONFIG_DB sonic-buildimage #27903

SAI defines End, End.X, End.T, End.DX4/DX6, End.DT4/DT6/DT46, End.B6.Encaps(.Red) and their uSID variants, but no L2 behaviors (End.DX2, End.DT2U/DT2M), so EVPN over SRv6 has no data plane in SONiC. See the SRv6 Support Matrix for the full list.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• ASIC data plane via SAI — srv6orch turns APP_DB entries into SAI my_sid and sidlist objects. The Linux kernel's seg6 data plane is not what forwards traffic on a SONiC switch.
  • FRRouting control plane — fpmsyncd carries SRv6 routes from FRR's zebra into APP_DB. SONiC's FRR container runs bgpd, staticd and ospfd (OSPFv2) but not isisd or ospf6d, so SIDs come from BGP (L3VPN) or from static configuration, not from an IGP.
  • Static configuration — since 202505, SRV6_MY_LOCATORS and SRV6_MY_SIDS in CONFIG_DB are translated by bgpcfgd into FRR static SIDs. This is the model used for AI back-end fabrics; see SRv6 AI Fabric Design.

docs.title: How to Read This Matrix
docs.text:
• Version numbers are the first release that a source documents for the feature (Cisco "Release x.y.z introduced", Juniper Feature Explorer "introduced in", kernel merge release, project release notes). A blank version on a ✓ means the feature is documented, but we found no first-release statement. Hardware matters: a feature introduced in a release is often limited to some platforms or line cards — the footnote says which.
  • Classic and uSID. A ✓ on an endpoint behavior means the platform implements it in at least one form: full-length SIDs (RFC 8986) or its NEXT-C-SID / uSID flavor (uN, uA, uDT46…). The footnote notes when only one form exists. See uSID Compression.
  • ◐ Partial means the feature exists with a significant restriction that is stated in the footnote (one form only, static configuration only, ASIC-dependent, preview).
  • Control-plane rows need the protocol to carry SRv6 information, not just to run over IPv6. A data-plane-only component (the Linux kernel, VPP) is ✗ there by design: pair it with a routing suite such as FRRouting.
  • Not listed ≠ not supported. Vendors ship features faster than documentation catches up. If you know better, tell us — see below.

docs.title: Cisco IOS-XR SRv6 support
docs.text: IOS-XR has had SRv6 since 6.6.1 (full-length SIDs, IS-IS, TI-LFA, L3VPN, OAM) and uSID (F3216) since 7.3.1; most later features are built on uSID: EVPN-VPWS 7.3.2, EVPN E-LAN 7.5.2, End.DT46 7.8.1. Cisco 8000 needs Q200-based hardware and ASR 9000 third-generation line cards or later. Gaps: no SRv6 Tree-SID (Tree-SID is SR-MPLS only), no per-CE uDX4/uDX6 with uSID, no PCE-initiated SRv6 policies. Configuration guide →

docs.title: Cisco IOS-XE SRv6 support
docs.text: IOS-XE supports SRv6 uSID since 17.12.1a on the ASR 1000 and Catalyst 8000 edge routers: IS-IS, BGP L3VPN with per-VRF uDT4/uDT6, local SRv6-TE with dynamic paths, PM and OAM. TI-LFA and microloop avoidance came in 17.15.1a, Flex-Algo and IPv4 MVPN ingress replication in 17.18.1a. No EVPN over SRv6 and no binding SIDs are documented. Configuration guide →

docs.title: Juniper SRv6 support (Junos and Junos Evolved)
docs.text: Junos OS supports SRv6 on MX since 20.3R1 (classic SIDs, IS-IS, Flex-Algo, TI-LFA), with BGP services from 20.4R1. uSID (NEXT-C-SID only; REPLACE-C-SID is not supported) arrived in 23.2R1 on ACX7000 and 23.4R1 on MX; PTX10002-36QDD and PTX10008 follow in 24.x. Junos has the broadest documented service set among the vendors here, including EVPN-VPWS and E-LAN, PCEP and BGP-LS. Configuration guide →

docs.title: Arista EOS SRv6 support
docs.text: EOS is uSID-only: uN since 4.34.2F, static uA 4.35.2F, IS-IS SRv6 and Flex-Algo on 7280R4/7800R4 since 4.36.1F. Arista's public documentation covers transport behaviors; BGP L3VPN and EVPN RT5 over SRv6 have only been shown in EANTC interoperability tests, so those cells are ◐. H.Encaps.Red, USP and End.DX4/DX6 are listed as unsupported. Platform page →

docs.title: Nokia SR OS SRv6 support
docs.text: SR OS supports SRv6 since 21.5.R2 on FP4-based hardware, with classic and micro-segment (uSID) SIDs side by side. It covers L3VPN, EVPN-VPLS/VPWS/IFL, BGP SR Policy, TI-LFA and Tree-SID SRv6 multicast (25.3, with restrictions). It uses only the reduced headend behaviors and does not implement End.T, End.DX4/DX6, OSPFv3 SRv6 or RFC 9433. Platform page →

docs.title: Huawei VRP SRv6 support
docs.text: Huawei's NetEngine 8000 V800R025 configuration guide documents nearly every row: all main endpoint and headend behaviors, IS-IS and OSPFv3 SRv6, L3VPN/EVPN/global services, SRv6 TE Policy with PCEP and BGP, TI-LFA, microloop avoidance and Flex-Algo. Its compression is G-SRv6 (REPLACE-C-SID), with NEXT-C-SID available only as a 16-bit interop mode. Huawei's portal no longer publishes guides older than V800R023, so most cells have no first-release number.

docs.title: FRRouting SRv6 support
docs.text: FRR has signaled SRv6 L3VPN in BGP since 8.1, uSID since 8.5 and IS-IS SRv6 since 9.1; 10.6 added global-table services and 10.7 BGP-LS. Because it programs the Linux kernel, it inherits the kernel's gaps (no USP/USD, no End.DT2U/DT2M). SRv6 TI-LFA, Flex-Algo, OSPFv3, PCEP and EVPN over SRv6 are not in any release yet. Configuration guide →

docs.title: Linux kernel SRv6 support
docs.text: The kernel has had SRv6 encapsulation since 4.10 and endpoint behaviors since 4.14; End.DT4 (5.11), End.DT46 (5.14), H.Encaps.Red (6.0), NEXT-C-SID (6.1) and PSP (6.3) came later. It is a data plane only: control-plane rows are ✗ by design. Behavior-by-kernel table →

docs.title: SONiC SRv6 support
docs.text: SONiC programs SRv6 into the switch ASIC through SAI. It has carried SRv6 code since 202111, uSID since 202211 and static CONFIG_DB SIDs (rated Alpha) since 202505. Every data-plane cell is ◐ because forwarding depends on each vendor's SAI implementation. SAI has no L2 behaviors, and SONiC's FRR container does not run an IGP for SRv6. Platform page →

docs.title: FD.io VPP SRv6 support
docs.text: VPP has been an SRv6 software data plane since 17.04, with uN in 20.05, uA in 25.02 and the srv6-mobile plugin (GTP-U interworking) in 20.01. It has no routing protocols, no End.DT46 and only the PSP flavor.

docs.title: Cilium SRv6 support
docs.text: Open-source Cilium contains a hidden, beta SRv6 datapath since 1.13 (single-SID encapsulation and decapsulation to IPv4/IPv6) but no control plane to drive it. SRv6 L3VPN and uSID are features of Isovalent Enterprise for Cilium, which this column does not cover. Platform page →

docs.title: Other implementations
docs.text: zebra-rs and Vinbero are eBPF-based open-source SRv6 stacks with their own behavior tables; they are not yet columns here. Nokia SR Linux added SRv6 in 26.3 (see the Nokia page).

docs.title: Corrections and Additions
docs.text:
This matrix is maintained in the open. If you are a vendor, an operator or a contributor and a cell is wrong, outdated or unknown while you can point to a public source:

  • Open an issue: Report a support-matrix correction with the platform, capability, release and a link to the document that states it.
  • Or send a pull request: edit docs/implementations/support-matrix.yml — one line per cell, with a source. The table, footnotes and tooltips are generated from that file.

We accept public vendor documentation, release notes, feature explorers, source code and RFC implementation reports. We do not accept marketing claims without a document behind them, and we will not mark a feature supported because a roadmap says it is coming.

docs.title: SRv6 with Vinbero (eBPF/Go)
docs.text:
Vinbero is an SRv6 implementation in two Go binaries: vinberod, a daemon that owns an eBPF data plane and an in-process BGP speaker, and vinbero, a CLI that drives it over Connect RPC. Forwarding happens in eBPF; the control plane exists to populate its maps.

Its coverage runs in two directions the other open-source stacks rarely take: the mobile user plane (RFC 9433 GTP-U ⇄ SRv6, signalled by BGP MUP) and service programming proxies that put SR-unaware appliances inside an SRv6 chain. Two gaps come with that. There is no IGP, so the underlay is plain IPv6 routing and BGP carries every service. RFC 9800 SID compression is on the roadmap and not implemented.

Versions

Facts on this page reflect Vinbero 0.1.1, Apache-2.0 licensed: takehaya/vinbero. The eBPF objects are load-tested in CI on kernels 6.1, 6.6, 6.12, and 7.0; the documented floor is Linux 5.15.

docs.title: Supported SRv6 Behaviors
docs.text:
Many of these behaviors have a runnable scenario under examples/, built from network namespaces with setup, test, and teardown scripts, and the BGP services are verified against FRRouting in CI with containerlab.

Group Behaviors Status Headend H.Encaps, H.Encaps.L2, H.Insert (all .Red) Endpoint End, End.X, End.T, End.DT4/6/46, End.DX4/6 Endpoint (L2) End.DX2, End.DX2V, End.DT2U, End.DT2M Binding SID End.B6.Encaps, End.B6.Insert (both .Red) Mobile user plane (RFC 9433) H.M.GTP4.D, H.M.GTP6.D, End.M.GTP6.D/.D.Di, End.M.GTP4.E, End.M.GTP6.E, Args.Mob.Session Service programming End.AS (static), End.AD (dynamic), End.AM (masquerading), End.AN (SR-aware) Flavors PSP / USP / USD Compression (RFC 9800) NEXT-C-SID (uSID), REPLACE-C-SID, End.LBS/XLBS Other End.BM, End.NSH, End.Replicate, End.MAP, End.Limit

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
One XDP program per interface dispatches behaviors through PROG_ARRAY tail calls, one slot per behavior. Reserved slots take operator-supplied XDP plugins registered at runtime, each configured per SID from JSON marshalled through the plugin's own BTF. A separate and much smaller TC program handles BUM replication, because bpf_clone_redirect exists only in TC.

Packets enter through an ingress front door that maps {ifindex, vlan} to a VRF, then take one of three paths: an LPM lookup in the local SID table, which yields a behavior and its per-SID parameters; an LPM lookup in the headend tables, which encapsulates towards a service SID after resolving an SR Policy if the route carries a color; or the L2 tables. A headend entry can point at a group of up to eight weighted paths, chosen by a hash of the inner flow and masked by a liveness bitmap that a userspace prober updates for fast reroute. That same hash goes into the outer flow label (RFC 6437), because every encapsulated packet between one pair of PEs otherwise shares an outer source and destination, which pins a whole site-to-site tunnel to one transit ECMP path.

One deliberate split: Vinbero holds no per-VRF IP routing table in eBPF. End.DT4/DT6/DT46 decapsulate and hand the inner packet to the kernel VRF device the SID names, and the kernel FIB does the lookup. eBPF owns what the kernel cannot do: the SRv6 service tables, the L2 tables, and the GTP behaviors.

docs.title: Control Plane
docs.text:
GoBGP v4 runs as a library inside vinberod (--bgp-enabled), so a received route becomes an eBPF map write inside a single process, with no sidecar. Each entry carries an owner tag, so a withdrawal removes what that route installed and leaves an operator's static entries in place.

Address family What it programs Reference VPNv4 / VPNv6 RD/RT demux, SRv6 Service TLV (incl. §4 SID-structure transposition) to H.Encaps towards the remote End.DT4/DT6 RFC 9252 EVPN (L2VPN) RT2 remote MACs, RT3 BUM peers (End.DT2M), RT4 Ethernet Segment with RFC 8584 DF election and Local-Bias split horizon, RT1 aliasing RFC 9252, RFC 7432, RFC 8584 SR Policy (SAFI 73) {color, endpoint} to a transport SID list, weighted segment lists, color steering in the data plane RFC 9256 BGP MUP (SAFI 85) ISD/DSD segment discovery and T1ST/T2ST sessions to GTP downlink H.Encaps and uplink F-TEID entries draft-mpmz-bess-mup-safi IPv6 unicast Injected into the kernel FIB RFC 4760

Route targets bind per family and per direction in one command, vinbero vrf-bgp bind --vrf vrf100 --rt vpnv4:65100:100:both, which drives both import filtering and auto-advertise: connected and static prefixes, EVPN RT2/RT3/RT4 from the bridge lifecycle, local SR Policies, and local MUP routes.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/takehaya/vinbero/main/scripts/install_vinbero.sh | sudo bash
sudo vinberod -c vinbero.yml   # --bgp-enabled to start the BGP speaker

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
vinbero.yml declares only what must exist at boot: which interfaces get XDP (internal.devices), the attach mode (internal.bpf.device_mode, either driver or generic for veth labs), the RPC bind address, and optional map pinning that carries data-plane state across a restart. Everything else is created at runtime.

# L3VPN: a VRF is one object (kernel device + vrf_id + ingress membership)
vinbero vrf create --name vrf100 --table-id 100 --members eth2 --enable-l3mdev-rule
vinbero sid create --trigger-prefix fc00:3::3/128 --action END_DT4 --vrf-name vrf100

# EVPN: a bridge domain behind an L2 VRF facet
vinbero vrf bridge-attach --vrf evi-100 --name br100 --bd-id 100 --members eth1
vinbero sid create --trigger-prefix fc00:2::2/128 --action END_DT2 --bd-id 100 --bridge-name br100

# Static headend (BGP writes the equivalent entries once a session is up)
vinbero hv4 create --trigger-prefix 10.2.0.0/24 --src-addr fc00:1::1 \
    --segments fc00:2::2,fc00:3::3

vinbero sid list && vinbero stats show

A VRF cannot be deleted while a SID, an ingress access circuit, or a BGP binding still references it: the daemon refuses and names the reference.

docs.title: SRv6 with zebra-rs (eBPF)
docs.text:
zebra-rs is a BGP, OSPF, and IS-IS routing stack written from scratch in Rust, with SRv6, SR-MPLS, L3VPN, and EVPN extensions. Its eBPF data plane is cradle-rs — an XDP/TC forwarding engine built on aya (pure Rust, no clang/libbpf) that zebra-rs launches and programs directly from its routing state.

The combination is an open-source SRv6 router: every route the protocols compute — IS-IS SRv6 locators, BGP L3VPN service SIDs, EVPN MAC routes — is installed into eBPF maps in addition to the Linux kernel FIB. Several SRv6 behaviors that the mainline kernel cannot forward at all (EVPN L2 decap, REPLACE-C-SID, egress protection, P2MP replication) run only on the eBPF path.

Versions

Facts on this page reflect zebra-rs 26.7.7 with the bundled cradle-rs 0.9.8 engine, BDD-tested on Linux 6.8. Both projects are AGPL-licensed: zebra-rs · cradle-rs.

docs.title: Why zebra-rs + cradle-rs?
docs.text:
Cilium brought SRv6 to eBPF for Kubernetes, but its BGP control plane only advertises routes — it never installs learned routes into the data path. zebra-rs approaches it from the routing side: a full multi-protocol routing stack (IS-IS, OSPFv3, BGP with VPNv4/VPNv6/EVPN/SR Policy address families) is the source of truth, and the eBPF engine is simply its FIB.

What makes it distinctive:

  • Learned routes program eBPF. IS-IS SRv6 locators, BGP L3VPN (VPNv4/VPNv6 with SRv6 SIDs), and BGP EVPN over SRv6 all land in the eBPF FIB through a gRPC tee — the direction Cilium's BGP control plane doesn't support.
  • The widest open-source behavior set. The full RFC 8986 catalog including End.T, End.DX2/DX2V, End.DT2U/DT2M, End.B6.Encaps, plus both RFC 9800 compression flavors (NEXT-C-SID and REPLACE-C-SID), the PSP/USP/USD flavors, End.M egress protection, and RFC 9524 End.Replicate.
  • A reverse channel. The data plane's MAC learning streams back up (WatchFdb), driving EVPN Type-2 origination and withdrawal — the eBPF data plane is a control-plane participant, not just a sink.
  • Rust end to end. Control plane, user-space loader, and the eBPF programs themselves are Rust (aya); no clang or libbpf in the build.

docs.title: Supported SRv6 Behaviors
docs.text: All rows marked supported are BDD-proven in the projects' test suites (feature names like cradle_srv6, cradle_srv6_usid, isis_srv6_base, l3vpn_bgp_v6 run the actual daemons in network namespaces and assert forwarding).

docs.title: Headend
docs.text: Behavior Notes Status H.Encaps Multi-SID SRH imposition (TC stage) H.Encaps.Red The default — single SID means no SRH on the wire H.Encaps.L2 / L2.Red MAC-in-SRv6 (next-header 143) for EVPN H.Insert TI-LFA repair imposition (IPv6)

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: Behavior Notes Status End, End.X, End.T SRH walk, adjacency cross-connect, table-scoped lookup End.DT4 / DT6 / DT46 Per-VRF decap; End.DT46 is the BGP L3VPN service SID End.DX4 / DX6 Decap + cross-connect to the CE adjacency End.DX2 / DX2V EVPN VPWS E-Line; DX2V demuxes the inner 802.1Q VID End.DT2U / DT2M EVPN unicast bridge / BUM flood (eBPF only) End.B6.Encaps / .Red Binding SID: End walk + policy push End.M Mirror SID egress protection (draft-ietf-rtgwg-srv6-egress-protection) End.Replicate RFC 9524 SR P2MP replication segment End.BM, End.S, End.AN/AS/AD/AM Service programming out of scope

docs.title: Compression (RFC 9800) and Flavors
docs.text: Feature Notes Status NEXT-C-SID (uSID): uN, uA, uA (LIB), uT, uDT4/6/46, uDX4/6 16-bit micro-SIDs, blocks 16/32/48 REPLACE-C-SID: End, End.X 32/16-bit C-SIDs — container walk + DA index argument. eBPF only — Linux 6.8 has no REPLACE seg6local op PSP / USP / USD RFC 8986 §4.16 flavors on End / End.X / uN / uA uB6

docs.title: One Routing Stack, Two FIBs
docs.text:
zebra-rs runs as a single tokio-based process; each protocol is an async task feeding a central RIB. Turning on the eBPF data plane is two config knobs:

system {
  ebpf {
    enabled true;
  }
}
interface enp0s6 {
  ebpf {
    enabled true;
  }
}

system ebpf enabled true makes zebra-rs spawn and supervise the cradle engine as a managed child process (crash → respawn with backoff, full FIB state replayed into the fresh instance) and tees every route install to it over gRPC (cradle.v1, default endpoint unix:cradle/grpc). interface <name> ebpf enabled true attaches the XDP + TC programs to that interface; the port follows the interface's VRF binding.

docs.title: XDP for Decap, TC for Encap
docs.text:
cradle-rs compiles one fully-inlined eBPF program per hook and splits SRv6 across them deliberately:

Stage SRv6 work Why there XDP (cradle_xdp) All endpoint behaviors: End SRH walk, uN shift-and-forward, End.DT*/DX* decap, End.DT2U/DT2M L2 decap, End.M, End.B6 policy push — plus MAC-in-SRv6 L2 encap Native XDP re-runs eth_type_trans after the header adjustment, so the decapsulated inner packet enters TC with a correct skb->protocol TC (cradle_tc) H.Encaps / H.Encaps.Red / H.Insert imposition, FIB forwarding, and the End.Replicate clone (bpf_clone_redirect is TC-only) Encap egress needs an explicit L2 rewrite — bpf_redirect_neigh would build the L2 header from the stale inner skb->protocol

A metadata channel (CradleXdpMeta) carries the VRF or bridge-domain from an XDP decap to the TC forwarding lookup, guarded by a per-instance random cookie so stale metadata can't cross a veth hop into a neighbor's TC stage.

docs.title: SRv6 eBPF Maps
docs.text: eBPF Map Key Value Purpose SRV6_LOCALSID SID (LPM trie) behavior, flavors, VRF, nexthop, SID structure Local SID table, probed before the IPv6 FIB SRV6_ENCAP Nexthop ID Segment list (≤6 SIDs) + encap mode Per-nexthop H.Encaps / H.Insert state SRV6_ENCAP_SRC — IPv6 address Outer source address for imposition FIB4_VRF / FIB6_VRF VRF + prefix (LPM) FIB entry Inner lookup for End.DT4/DT6/DT46 FDB MAC + VLAN port or remote End.DT2U SID EVPN L2: remote entries carry the peer's SID XCONNECT / XCONNECT_VLAN AC ifindex / (table, VID) Remote End.DX2/DX2V SID VPWS E-Line ingress REPL_SEG / REPL_SID SID / ifindex Branch list / per-copy target RFC 9524 replication tree, EVPN BUM slots MIRROR Context + prefix (LPM) behavior, VRF End.M egress-protection mirror contexts

docs.title: Control Plane
docs.text:
Producer What it programs Reference IS-IS SRv6 Locator TLV 27 (with Algorithm for Flex-Algo), End/uN node SIDs, End.X/uA adjacency SIDs, End.T/uT for VRF-bound locators, SID Structure sub-sub-TLV RFC 9352, RFC 9350 OSPFv3 SRv6-Locator-LSA (0xA02A), End/uN + SID Structure, per-adjacency End.X/uA in the E-Router-LSA RFC 9513 BGP L3VPN VPNv4/VPNv6 with a per-VRF End.DT46 SID in the Prefix-SID attribute (SRv6 L3 Service TLV); VPN-IPv4 over an IPv6 next-hop RFC 9252, RFC 8669, RFC 8950 BGP EVPN Type-2 → End.DT2U, Type-3 → End.DT2M + BUM replication slots, Type-5 → per-VRF End.DT46, VPWS Type-1 → End.DX2; MAC mobility sequencing fed by the WatchFdb learn/age stream RFC 9252, RFC 8214, RFC 9136 BGP SR Policy Binding SID (SAFI 73) → End.B6.Encaps, color-based steering to a BSID RFC 9256, RFC 9830 TI-LFA Repair segment lists as H.Insert/H.Encaps backups, per-Flex-Algo TI-LFA, PSP on the repair carrier RFC 9855 Egress protection Mirror SID (End.M) advertised in IS-IS; live L3VPN failover on egress PE death draft-ietf-rtgwg-srv6-egress-protection

One deliberate design detail: the per-VRF BGP service-SID functions are allocated from a band (0x0040–0xDFFF) kept below the IS-IS End.X/uA range (0xE000+), following the IOS-XR uSID GIB/LIB convention — so BGP and IS-IS share a single locator without collisions.

eBPF-only behaviors

zebra-rs installs the classic behaviors (End, End.X, uN, uA, End.T, End.DT4/6/46, End.DX4/6, End.B6.Encaps, H.Encaps) into the kernel as seg6/seg6local routes and the eBPF engine. But End.DT2U/DT2M (EVPN L2), End.DX2/DX2V (VPWS), End.M, End.Replicate, uT, and the REPLACE-C-SID behaviors have no mainline-kernel equivalent — for those, cradle-rs is the only data plane. EVPN over SRv6 on Linux effectively requires it.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Prebuilt .deb packages exist for Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 / 26.04 (x86_64 and ARM64):

curl -fsSL https://zebra.rs/install.sh | bash

The cradle-rs engine ships as a separate Debian package that zebra-rs recommends and pulls in automatically; zebra-rs finds it at /usr/bin/cradle with no further setup. Building cradle-rs from source needs a nightly Rust toolchain with rust-src and bpf-linker — no clang or libbpf.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration is YANG-modeled with a candidate/running commit model, and the same tree can be expressed as Cisco-style CLI, YAML, JSON, or set commands (vtyctl apply -f zebra.yaml). The snippets below come from the project's book and BDD suite — they are validated, running configurations.

docs.title: Step 1 — Define an SRv6 Locator
docs.text:
segment-routing {
  locator LOC1 {
    prefix fcbb:bbbb:1::/48;
    behavior usid;
  }
}

behavior usid selects RFC 9800 NEXT-C-SID (micro-SID) format; behavior replace selects REPLACE-C-SID; omitting it gives classic full-length RFC 8986 SIDs. Optional per-locator flavor {psp|usp|usd} and vrf <name> (which turns the node SID into End.T/uT) are supported.

docs.title: Step 2 — Advertise it in the IGP
docs.text:
router {
  isis {
    net 49.0000.0000.0000.0001.00;
    is-type level-2-only;
    segment-routing {
      srv6 {
        locator LOC1;
      }
    }
    interface enp0s6 {
      circuit-type level-2-only;
      ipv6 {
        enabled true;
      }
      network-type point-to-point;
    }
  }
}

(OSPFv3 is analogous: router ospfv3 { segment-routing { srv6 { locator LOC1; } } }. OSPFv2 cannot carry SRv6 — it is IPv6-only on the wire.)

docs.title: Step 3 — BGP L3VPN over SRv6
docs.text:
router bgp {
  global {
    as 65000;
  }
  segment-routing {
    srv6 {
      locator LOC1;
    }
  }
  vrf vrf1 {
    rd 65000:1;
    encapsulation srv6;
    neighbor 10.100.0.2 {
      remote-as 65001;
    }
    afi-safi ipv4 {
      network 192.168.5.0/24;
    }
    afi-safi ipv6 {
      network 2001:db8:5::/64;
    }
  }
}

vrf vrf1 {
  ipv4 {
    route-target {
      import 65000:1;
      export 65000:1;
    }
  }
  ipv6 {
    route-target {
      import 65000:1;
      export 65000:1;
    }
  }
}

encapsulation srv6 switches the VRF from MPLS labels to a per-VRF End.DT46 SID — one SID serves both VPNv4 and VPNv6. EVPN L2 uses the same pattern (afi-safi evpn + encapsulation srv6) to advertise End.DT2U/End.DT2M SIDs.

docs.title: Step 4 — Enable the eBPF Data Plane
docs.text:
system {
  ebpf {
    enabled true;
  }
}
interface enp0s6 {
  ebpf {
    enabled true;
  }
}

docs.title: Step 5 — Verify
docs.text:
zebra> show ebpf
eBPF data plane
  System ebpf:     enabled
  FIB tee:         enabled
  Engine:          managed (pid 168157), up 42s
  Engine restarts: 1
  ...

zebra> show ebpf srv6        # SRv6 local SIDs and transit encaps
zebra> show ebpf ipv6 vrf vrf1
zebra> show ebpf stats       # datapath counters, per-behavior

Every show ebpf command takes a trailing json for machine-readable output.

docs.title: Full Traffic Walk
docs.text:
An L3VPN packet through a uSID fabric — ingress imposition in TC, everything else in XDP:

docs.title: SRv6（IPv6 Segment Routing）の概要
docs.text:
SRv6（Segment Routing over IPv6）は、Segment Routing v6やIPv6 Segment Routingとも呼ばれ、Segment Routingアーキテクチャ（RFC 8402）のIPv6データプレーンです。転送の命令をIPv6パケットのヘッダーに直接エンコードします。MPLSラベルや、LDP・RSVP-TEのようなシグナリングプロトコルに頼る代わりに、128ビットのネイティブなIPv6アドレスを**セグメント識別子（SID）**として使い、ネットワークの経路と振る舞いをプログラムします。

送信元ノードは、パケットの経路と各ホップでの処理を定義する、順序付きのセグメントリストを作成します。アクティブなセグメントはIPv6の宛先アドレスに入り、セグメントが複数ある場合は残りが**Segment Routing Header（SRH）**で運ばれます。さらにuSIDによる圧縮を使えば、経路全体が宛先アドレスだけに収まり、SRHがまったく不要になることも珍しくありません。トランジットルーターは宛先アドレスに基づいて転送するだけです。これにより、トラフィックエンジニアリング、VPNサービス、高速迂回（FRR）、サービスファンクションチェイニングを、通常のIPv6ネットワーク上で実現できます。

従来のMPLSではなくSRv6を選ぶ理由

  • 運用のシンプル化：MPLSラベルの管理、LDP、RSVPが不要
  • ネイティブIPv6：既存のIPv6データプレーンをそのまま使い、オーバーレイが不要
  • ネットワークプログラマビリティ：SRv6のFunction（End、End.DT4、End.DX6など）で振る舞いを定義できる
  • スケーラビリティ：128ビットのSID空間で大規模ネットワークに対応
  • データプレーンの統一：トランスポート、VPN、トラフィックエンジニアリングを単一のプロトコルスタックで実現

docs.title: AIのためのSRv6：完全ガイド
docs.text:
Read in English · Leer en español

SRv6は、AIネットワークの基盤となるプロトコルになりました。 GPUの学習用ファブリックでは、送信側のNICがすべてのパケットの正確な経路を、16ビットのuSIDのリストとしてIPv6の宛先アドレスに書き込みます。スイッチはルーティングプロトコルを使わず、スタティックなテーブルだけで転送します。トランスポートは数百本の明示的な経路にトラフィックを分散（スプレー）し、障害の起きた経路をマイクロ秒単位で切り離します。データセンター間では、SRv6のトラフィックエンジニアリングがAIトラフィックをWAN上で制御します。OpenAI、Microsoft、OracleはAI学習用ファブリックでSRv6を運用し、MetaはAIクラスターを相互接続するバックボーンで、Alibaba CloudはAIコンピューティングネットワーク全体でSRv6を使っています。

要点（2026年10月時点）

  • 商用運用：スタティックSRv6上のMRC （英語） が、OpenAIの最大規模のGB200クラスター、MicrosoftのFairwaterスーパーコンピューター、そしてテキサス州アビリーンを含むOracleのOCIクラスターで、フロンティアモデルの学習に使われています。報告されているジョブは75,000 GPUに達し、ファブリックは2階層で131,072 GPUを収容する設計です。
  • バックエンドにBGPなし：スイッチが持つのは、設置時に一度だけ書き込む小さなスタティックuSIDテーブルです。障害対応はNICに移ります。
  • 40バイト：uSIDを使えば、経路全体が1つのIPv6宛先アドレスに収まり、Segment Routing Header（SRH）は不要です。
  • Scale-Across：Meta（リージョナルバックボーン、2026年10月からSRv6 TEを商用運用）とAlibaba（ジョブ単位のSRv6 TEを行う専用の「eCore for AI」）が、AIサイト間でSRv6を使っています。
  • 標準化：データプレーンはRFC 8986とRFC 9800、AIでの使い方はdraft-filsfils-srv6ops-srv6-ai-backend （英語）（-05、Cisco、OpenAI、Microsoft、Oracle、IBM、NVIDIA、Arrcusの共著）、トランスポートはOCP MRC 1.0、スイッチソフトウェアはSONiC 202505以降で規定されています。

docs.title: SRv6がAIネットワークに適している理由
docs.text:
1. ハッシュではなく決定的な経路。 AIの学習は少数の巨大な同期フローで構成され、ECMPにとって最悪のケースです。SRv6では送信側がすべてのパケットを既知の経路に載せるため、ハッシュの衝突がなく、経路の切り替えも正確です。SRv6 vs ECMP、Adaptive Routing、Ultra Ethernet （英語） を参照してください。
  2. スタティックでシンプルなファブリック。 スタティックなuSIDルートが、BGPとその再収束を置き換えます。MRCを運用する事業者は、学習チームと調整せずにスパインスイッチを再起動しています。
  3. 実態に即した可視性。 データと同じuSID経路を使うプローブは、データが経験するものをそのまま検証します。OpenAIのClustermapperは、すべてのリンクを1ミリ秒ごとにプローブしています。AI Fabric Telemetry （英語） を参照してください。
  4. 最小限のオーバーヘッド。 uSID（RFC 9800）は、最大6ホップを128ビットのアドレス1つに詰め込みます。コストは40バイトの外側IPv6ヘッダー1つだけで、主流のスイッチASICがラインレートで処理します。
  5. GPUからWANまで1つの技術。 同じSRv6データプレーンが、バックエンドファブリック、データセンターのフロントエンド、DC間バックボーンを担い、DCのエッジにMPLSゲートウェイは必要ありません。Scale-Across （英語） を参照してください。
  6. オープンでマルチベンダー。 NICはNVIDIA、AMD、Broadcom、スイッチはNVIDIA、Arista（Broadcom搭載）、Cisco Silicon One、そしてオープンソースのSONiC、SAI、FRRが使われています。

docs.title: AIネットワークでSRv6は何に使われていますか？
docs.text: AIネットワークでのSRv6の用途は2つあります。GPU学習クラスターの内部では、NICがSRv6のuSIDを使って、バックエンドファブリックを通るすべてのパケットの正確な経路を選びます。これによりECMPのハッシュ衝突がなくなり、スイッチはダイナミックルーティングなしで動作でき、すべての経路を検証できるようになります。データセンター間では、SRv6のトラフィックエンジニアリングが、AIトラフィックを適切な遅延と容量を持つ経路に誘導します。

docs.title: OpenAIはSRv6を使っていますか？
docs.text: はい。OpenAIの最大規模のGB200学習クラスターは、スタティックなSRv6 uSIDソースルーティング上でMRC（Multipath Reliable Connection）を使っており、スイッチのダイナミックルーティングは無効化されています。OpenAI、Microsoft、AMD、Broadcom、NVIDIAが2026年5月にこの設計を公表し、OpenAIは2026年10月のOCP Global Summitで、SRv6ベースの監視システムClustermapperを発表しました。

docs.title: SRv6がAIの学習に適しているのはなぜですか？
docs.text: AIの学習は少数の非常に大きな同期フローを送るため、フロー単位のハッシュでは衝突が起き、最も遅い経路がジョブ全体を遅くします。SRv6を使えば、送信側が各パケットを明示的な経路に載せ、数百本の経路にスプレーし、障害の起きた経路をマイクロ秒単位で切り離せます。スイッチはスタティックでシンプルなまま保たれ、uSIDによってオーバーヘッドは40バイトのIPv6ヘッダー1つに抑えられます。

docs.title: SRv6とUltra Ethernetの違いは何ですか？
docs.text: Ultra Ethernetは、ネットワーク層を変更せずに、スイッチがハッシュするエントロピー値を使ってパケットをスプレーするトランスポートを定義しています。SRv6はネットワーク層のソースルーティング技術で、各エントロピー値を明示的な経路に対応付けることができます。両者は補完関係にあり、MRCはUltra Ethernet由来のトランスポート機能とSRv6のソースルーティングを組み合わせています。

docs.title: AIファブリック向けにSRv6をサポートしているスイッチは？
docs.text: 公開されている導入事例では、NVIDIA Spectrum-4とSpectrum-5（CumulusまたはSONiC）、Broadcom Tomahawk 5上のArista EOS、SONiCを動かすCisco Silicon Oneシステムが使われています。SONiCはリリース202505から、スタティックなSRv6 uSID設定をサポートしています。

docs.title: AIデータセンター間でもSRv6は使われていますか？
docs.text: はい。Metaは、データセンターキャンパスとAIクラスターを相互接続するリージョナルバックボーンでSRv6のトラフィックエンジニアリングを使っています。Alibaba Cloudは、ジョブ単位のトラフィックエンジニアリングを行う、複数サイトにまたがるAI学習専用のSRv6ネットワークを運用しています。

docs.title: SIDの構造
docs.text:
Read in English · Leer en español

SRv6の**Segment Identifier（SID）**は128ビットの値で、通常のIPv6アドレスと同じ形式で表記します。SIDは、ノードの位置と、そのノードで実行するビヘイビアの両方をエンコードしています。

docs.title: SRv6 SIDの構成
docs.text:
|<------------ 128 bits ------------->|
|  Locator      | Function | Arguments|
|<-- L bits --->|<-F bits->|<-A bits->|
フィールド 説明 一般的なサイズ Locator ノードを識別するルーティング可能なプレフィックス 40〜64ビット Function ローカルのビヘイビア（End、End.DT4など）を識別 16〜24ビット Arguments Functionに渡すオプションのパラメータ 0〜48ビット

docs.title: 例
docs.text:
SID:  5f00:0:1::100

Breakdown:
  Locator:  5f00:0:1::/48   (identifies the node)
  Function: ::100            (End.DT4 - decap and lookup in IPv4 table)
  Args:     (none)

この例では、Locator 5f00:0:1::/48がノードを識別し、Function ::100がEnd.DT4（デカプセル化してIPv4テーブルを検索）を表します。Argumentsはありません。

LocatorはIGPの経路として広告される

Locatorのブロックは、IGP（IS-ISまたはOSPFv3）で通常のIPv6経路として広告されます。これにより、ネットワーク内のSRv6対応ノードすべてへの到達性が確保されます。

docs.title: IANAが割り当てたSRv6 SIDブロック（5f00::/16）
docs.text:
RFC 9602（2024年10月）は、SRv6のSID専用のIPv6プレフィックスを割り当てています。IANAはこのブロックをIPv6 Unicast Address Registryから割り当て、IPv6 Special-Purpose Address Registryに登録しました。

項目 値 Address Block 5f00::/16 Name Segment Routing (SRv6) SIDs RFC RFC 9602 Allocation Date 2024-04 Source True Destination True Forwardable True Globally Reachable False Reserved-by-Protocol False

5f00::/16はSRドメイン内では転送可能ですが、グローバルには到達不可能と明示されています。つまり、これらのアドレスを宛先とするパケットがパブリックなインターネットを通過してはいけません。

このブロック内での典型的な割り当て階層は次のとおりです。

5f00::/16                          <- IANA SRv6 SID block
  5f00:<domain>::/32               <- Operator / SR domain
    5f00:<domain>:<node>::/48      <- Node locator
      5f00:<domain>:<node>:<func>::/64  <- SID (locator + function)

docs.title: 事業者のGUAプレフィックスと5f00::/16の使い分け
docs.text:
RFC 9602は5f00::/16の使用を義務付けてはいません。事業者は、自社のグローバルユニキャストアドレス（GUA）のプレフィックスを引き続きSRv6のLocatorとして使えます。どちらの方式も有効です。

方式 プレフィックスの出どころ 長所 短所 IANAのSRv6ブロック 5f00::/16 パケットキャプチャやACLで一目でわかる。フィルタリングが簡単。GUAを消費しない グローバルにはルーティングされない。SRドメイン内でIGP/BGPによる明示的な広告が必要 事業者のGUA 事業者の/32や/48 事業者ネットワーク内ですでにルーティング可能。通常のIPv6到達性と兼用できる GUAを消費する。通常のIPv6トラフィックとSRv6トラフィックを見分けにくい

初期のSRv6導入事例の多く（China Mobile、ソフトバンクなど）は、事業者が割り当てたGUAプレフィックスを使っています。RFC 9602はそれを補完する選択肢で、特にグリーンフィールドの導入や、共通の識別しやすいプレフィックスによってフィルタリングが簡単になるドメイン間SRv6で役立ちます。

docs.title: ドメイン境界での5f00::/16のフィルタリング
docs.text:
5f00::/16を使う場合も自社のGUAを使う場合も、SRv6のSIDがSRドメインの外へ漏れないようにする必要があります。

Cisco IOS-XRJuniper JunosLinux (ip6tables) 
prefix-set DENY-SRV6
  5f00::/16 le 128
end-set

route-policy EBGP-IN
  if destination in DENY-SRV6 then
    drop
  endif
end-policy

policy-options {
    prefix-list SRV6-SID-SPACE {
        5f00::/16;
    }
    policy-statement REJECT-SRV6 {
        term deny-srv6 {
            from prefix-list SRV6-SID-SPACE;
            then reject;
        }
    }
}

ip6tables -A FORWARD -d 5f00::/16 -j DROP

事業者のGUAプレフィックスを使う場合も、同じ考え方を自社のLocatorのプレフィックス範囲に適用してください（RFC 8754 Section 5.1も参照）。

docs.title: SRHとパケットウォーク
docs.text:
Read in English · Leer en español

Segment Routing Header（SRH）がパケットレベルでどう動くかを理解することは、SRv6ネットワークの設計とトラブルシューティングに欠かせません。このページでは、その仕組みを一歩ずつ追っていきます。

docs.title: 主なフィールド
docs.text:
フィールド サイズ 説明 Next Header 8ビット 次のヘッダーの種類（例：41 = IPv6、4 = IPv4） Hdr Ext Len 8ビット 先頭8オクテットを除いたSRHの長さ（8オクテット単位） Routing Type 8ビット SRHでは常に4 Segments Left（SL） 8ビット セグメントリストのインデックスで、現在アクティブなセグメントを指す Last Entry 8ビット セグメントリストの最後の要素のインデックス（0始まり） Flags 8ビット 現在は未使用（予約） Tag 16ビット パケットのグルーピングやマーキング Segment List 各128ビット SIDの順序付きリスト。逆順で格納される

逆順に注意

セグメントリストは逆順でエンコードされます。Segment List[0]が最後に処理されるSIDで、Segment List[n]が最初に処理されるSIDです。Segments Leftはnから始まり、0に向かってデクリメントされます。

docs.title: パケットウォークの全体像
docs.text:
3ノード構成のSRv6ネットワークでパケットを追跡してみましょう。

Source (A) → Node B → Node C → Destination (D)

SRv6 SIDs:
  B::100  = End behavior on Node B
  C::200  = End.DT4 behavior on Node C (decap to IPv4)

B::100はノードBのEndビヘイビア、C::200はノードCのEnd.DT4ビヘイビア（デカプセル化してIPv4へ）です。

docs.title: ステップ1：Ingress（送信元A）
docs.text:
送信元Aは10.0.0.2宛てのIPv4パケットを受信し、B、Cの順に経由させる必要があります。

Original packet:
  [IPv4: 10.0.0.1 → 10.0.0.2][Payload]

After SRv6 encapsulation:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Outer IPv6 Header                         │
  │   Source:      A::1                       │
  │   Destination: B::100  ← Active SID      │
  │   Next Header: 43 (Routing)               │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ SRH                                       │
  │   Segments Left: 1                        │
  │   Last Entry:    1                        │
  │   Segment List[0]: C::200  (last SID)     │
  │   Segment List[1]: B::100  (first SID)    │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Inner IPv4 Header                         │
  │   10.0.0.1 → 10.0.0.2                    │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Payload                                   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

DA = アクティブSID

IPv6の宛先アドレス（DA）は、常に現在アクティブなSID（Segment List[Segments Left]）と一致します。

docs.title: ステップ2：トランジット（ノードB：Endビヘイビア）
docs.text:
ノードBがパケットを受信します。DAが自身のローカルSID B::100（Endビヘイビア）に一致するので、次の処理を行います。

  1. Segments Leftをデクリメント：1 → 0
  2. Segment List[0]をIPv6のDAにコピー：DA = C::200
  3. 新しいDAに基づいて転送
After Node B processing:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Outer IPv6 Header                         │
  │   Source:      A::1                       │
  │   Destination: C::200  ← Updated!        │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ SRH                                       │
  │   Segments Left: 0     ← Decremented!    │
  │   Last Entry:    1                        │
  │   Segment List[0]: C::200                 │
  │   Segment List[1]: B::100                 │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Inner IPv4: 10.0.0.1 → 10.0.0.2          │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Payload                                   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: ステップ3：Egress（ノードC：End.DT4ビヘイビア）
docs.text:
ノードCがパケットを受信します。DAが自身のローカルSID C::200（End.DT4ビヘイビア）に一致します。

  1. SL = 0なので、これが最後のセグメント
  2. デカプセル化：外側のIPv6ヘッダーとSRHを取り除く
  3. 指定されたVRFテーブルで内側のIPv4 DAをルックアップ
  4. 元のIPv4パケットを転送
After Node C processing:
  [IPv4: 10.0.0.1 → 10.0.0.2][Payload]  ← Original packet restored!

docs.title: ステップ4：配送
docs.text: 元のIPv4パケットは、SRv6を経由したことをまったく意識させずに宛先10.0.0.2へ届けられます。

docs.title: パケットウォークのシーケンス図
docs.text: 宛先ノードC (End.DT4)ノードB (End)送信元A宛先ノードC (End.DT4)ノードB (End)送信元A10.0.0.2宛てのIPv4パケットを受信カプセル化: IPv6(DA=B::100) + SRH[C::200, B::100] + IPv4B::100へ転送 (SL=1)B::100に一致 → EndビヘイビアSL: 1→0, DA: B::100→C::200C::200へ転送 (SL=0)C::200に一致 → End.DT4ビヘイビアデカプセル化し、VRFでIPv4をルックアップ元のIPv4パケットを転送

docs.title: PSP、USP、USDフレーバー
docs.text:
SRv6のエンドポイントは、SRHの扱い方を最適化するさまざまなフレーバーをサポートできます。

フレーバー 正式名称 説明 PSP Penultimate Segment Pop 最後から2番目のノード（SL=1）が、最後のセグメントへ転送する前にSRHを取り除く。Egressノードの負荷を減らせる USP Ultimate Segment Pop 最後のノード自身がSRHを取り除く USD Ultimate Segment Decap 最後のノードが外側のIPv6ヘッダーとSRHをまとめてデカプセル化する。End.DT4/DT6と組み合わせて使う

最も一般的なのはPSP

PSPはSRHの除去をEgress PEから肩代わりして効率を高めるため、広く使われています。最近の実装の多くはEnd with PSPまたはEnd with PSP-USP-USDを広告します。

docs.title: TLV付きのSRH
docs.text:
SRHは、セグメントリストの後ろにオプションのTLV（Type-Length-Value）オブジェクトを運べます。

TLV 説明 HMAC TLV SRHの暗号学的な認証 Padding TLV アライメントのためのパディング NSH Carrier TLV サービスチェイニング用のNSHメタデータを運ぶ

docs.title: Reduced Encapsulation（H.Encaps.Red）
docs.text:
H.Encaps.Red（Reduced Encapsulation、RFC 8986）は、経路の最初のSIDをセグメントリストから省くことでSRHを最適化します。最初のSIDはヘッドエンドがすでにIPv6のDAに入れているためです。これによりパケットごとに16バイトを節約でき、SIDが1つだけの経路ではSRH自体が不要になります。

Path: SID-1 → SID-2 → SID-3   (segment list is stored in reverse order)

H.Encaps:      SRH [SID-3, SID-2, SID-1], SL=2, DA = SID-1
H.Encaps.Red:  SRH [SID-3, SID-2],        SL=2, DA = SID-1  ← SID-1 only in the DA

H.Encaps.Redでは、SID-1はDAにだけ存在し、SRHには入りません。SLは省略しない場合と同じ値（2）から始まります。

docs.title: 確認コマンド
docs.text:
LinuxCisco IOS-XRJuniper 
# SRv6パケットをキャプチャ（Routing Header、Next Header 43）
tcpdump -i eth0 -vv 'ip6 proto 43'

# ローカルSIDテーブルを表示
ip -6 route show | grep seg6local

# tsharkでデコード
tshark -i eth0 -O ipv6 -Y 'ipv6.routing.type == 4'

show segment-routing srv6 sid
show cef ipv6 <SID> detail
debug segment-routing srv6 dataplane

show route table inet6.0 protocol srv6
show spring-traffic-engineering srv6-sid

docs.title: SRv6 vs SR-MPLS
docs.text:
Read in English · Leer en español

SRv6とSR-MPLSはどちらもSegment Routingを実装する方式ですが、使うデータプレーンが異なります。ここでは実務の観点から両者を比較します。

docs.title: 比較表
docs.text:
項目 SR-MPLS SRv6 データプレーン MPLS IPv6 セグメントID 20ビットのラベル 128ビットのIPv6アドレス SID空間 約100万ラベル 事実上無制限 カプセル化 MPLSラベルスタック SRv6 SRH（IPv6拡張ヘッダー） ネットワークプログラミング 限定的 豊富（End、End.X、End.DT4など） MTUへの影響 ラベルごとに4バイト IPv6 40B + 8B + SIDごとに16B 既存インフラ MPLS転送が必要 ネイティブIPv6を利用 シグナリング 不要（SRv6と同じ） 不要 成熟度 広く導入済み 急速に拡大中

SRv6のオーバーヘッドはもはや以前のものではない

SIDごとに16バイトという数字は従来のSRv6の場合です。uSID（RFC 9800）を使えば、16バイトのコンテナ1つに最大6つの命令を収められるため、SRv6のオーバーヘッドはMPLSのラベルスタックと同等かそれ以下になります。詳しくはuSIDを参照してください。

docs.title: どちらを選ぶべきか
docs.text:
SR-MPLSを選ぶケース

  • 既存のMPLSインフラがある
  • MTUのオーバーヘッドが懸念事項である
  • 主なユースケースがTEやVPNである

SRv6を選ぶケース

  • IPv6ネイティブなネットワークを新たに構築する
  • 高度なネットワークプログラマビリティが必要
  • シンプル化と将来性を重視する
  • MPLSを完全になくしたい

docs.title: uSID：SRv6のSID圧縮
docs.text:
Read in English · Leer en español

SRv6に対する初期の批判の1つがオーバーヘッドでした。SIDは1つあたり128ビット（16バイト）あり、5つのSIDからなるセグメントリストは、すべてのパケットに80バイトを追加します。**マイクロSID（uSID）**は、複数のセグメント命令を128ビットのSID 1つに詰め込むことで、この問題を解決します。

docs.title: 課題
docs.text:
従来のSRv6では、セグメントリストのホップごとに16バイトかかります。

Classic SRv6 (5 SIDs = 80 bytes overhead):
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SRH: Segment List                             │
│   [0]: fc00:0:5::1  (16 bytes)               │
│   [1]: fc00:0:4::1  (16 bytes)               │
│   [2]: fc00:0:3::1  (16 bytes)               │
│   [3]: fc00:0:2::1  (16 bytes)               │
│   [4]: fc00:0:1::1  (16 bytes)               │
│                          Total: 80 bytes      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

短いパケットや遅延に敏感なトラフィックでは、このオーバーヘッドは無視できません。

docs.title: 構造
docs.text: 要素 サイズ 説明 uSID Block 32ビット ドメイン内のすべてのuSIDに共通のプレフィックス（例：fcbb:bbbb） uSID 各16ビット ノードとビヘイビアを識別する個々のマイクロ命令 End-of-Container 16ビット（0000） コンテナ内の有効なuSIDの終わりを示す

docs.title: 動作の仕組み
docs.text:
uSIDコンテナの処理は、シンプルな**シフト＆ルックアップ（shift-and-lookup）**です。

ステップ1 - Ingressが受信:
  DA = fcbb:bbbb:0001:0002:0003:0000:0000:0000
                  ^^^^
                  アクティブuSID → ノード1

ステップ2 - ノード1がuSID 0001を処理し、左にシフト:
  DA = fcbb:bbbb:0002:0003:0000:0000:0000:0000
                  ^^^^
                  アクティブuSID → ノード2

ステップ3 - ノード2がuSID 0002を処理し、左にシフト:
  DA = fcbb:bbbb:0003:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000
                  ^^^^
                  アクティブuSID → ノード3

ステップ4 - ノード3がuSID 0003を処理し、左にシフト:
  DA = fcbb:bbbb:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000
                  ^^^^
                  End-of-Container (0000) → SRHの次のエントリへ

docs.title: オーバーヘッドの比較
docs.text:
シナリオ 従来のSRv6 uSID 削減率 SID 3つ 48バイト 16バイト 67% SID 6つ 96バイト 16バイト 83% SID 10個 160バイト 32バイト（コンテナ2つ） 80% SID 12個 192バイト 32バイト（コンテナ2つ） 83%

16バイトで6ホップ

uSIDコンテナ1つで、従来のSRv6がSID 1つに使うのと同じ領域に、最大6つのセグメント命令をエンコードできます。これにより、オーバーヘッドの点でSRv6はMPLSのラベルスタックと同等か、それ以上になります。

docs.title: uSIDとG-SRv6
docs.text:
2つの圧縮方式が登場し、現在はRFC 9800の下で統一されています。

項目 uSID（NEXT-C-SID） G-SRv6（REPLACE-C-SID） 提案元 Cisco、Bell Canada China Mobile、Huawei 処理方式 シフト＆ルックアップ リプレース＆ルックアップ uSIDのサイズ 16または32ビット 16または32ビット RFC RFC 9800 RFC 9800 採用状況 世界の複数の事業者 世界の複数の事業者

どちらもRFC 9800（SRv6 SID Compression）で標準化されており、相互運用性が確保されています。

docs.title: 設定例
docs.text:
Cisco IOS-XRLinux (iproute2) 
segment-routing
 srv6
  locators
   locator uSID-MAIN
    micro-segment behavior unode psp-usd
    prefix fcbb:bb01::/48
   !
  !
 !
!

# uSIDコンテナでカプセル化
ip route add 10.0.0.0/24 encap seg6 mode encap \
  segs fcbb:bbbb:0001:0002:0003:: dev eth0
